hints: Focus on what happens when each chloride meets water, does it just dissolve or does it react to release acid?
Recall that NaCl simply dissolves to give neutral ions, while SiCl4 hydrolyses completely to give HCl.
Remember that AlCl3 also gives an acidic solution by partial hydrolysis of the hydrated aluminium ion, so check what colour Universal Indicator shows in neutral versus strongly acidic solution.
walkthrough:
**Test-tube X with NaCl**

NaCl is an ionic chloride of a Group 1 metal. It just dissolves in water with no hydrolysis.

$$\text{NaCl(s) + aq} \rightarrow \text{Na}^{+}\text{(aq)} + \text{Cl}^{-}\text{(aq)}$$
The solution stays neutral at pH 7, so Universal Indicator stays green. Statement 1 is correct.

**Test-tube Y with SiCl4**

SiCl4 is a covalent tetrachloride. It reacts vigorously with water (complete hydrolysis) to form white solid silica and strong acid HCl.

$$\text{SiCl}_{4}\text{(l)} + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_{2}\text{(s)} + 4\text{HCl(aq)}$$
The HCl makes the solution strongly acidic with pH 1 to 2, so Universal Indicator turns red. Statement 2 is correct.

**Test-tube Z with AlCl3**

AlCl3 dissolves to give the hydrated ion $\text{[Al(H}_{2}\text{O)}_{6}\text{]}^{3+}$, which then loses a proton to water. This is partial hydrolysis.

$$\text{[Al(H}_{2}\text{O)}_{6}\text{]}^{3+}\text{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{[Al(H}_{2}\text{O)}_{5}\text{(OH)]}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}^{+}\text{(aq)}$$
The released $\text{H}^{+}$ makes the solution acidic with pH about 3, so Universal Indicator turns red-orange, described as red. Statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

Since statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, the combination that includes all three is the right choice.

options.A: Correct. All three statements are true. X is neutral and stays green, while both Y and Z become acidic and turn red due to complete hydrolysis of SiCl4 and partial hydrolysis of the aluminium aqua ion.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out statement 3. Many students think only SiCl4 hydrolyses, but forget that AlCl3 also hydrolyses to give an acidic solution.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out statement 1. NaCl does not hydrolyse, so its solution is neutral and the indicator correctly stays green.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. It wrongly suggests Y and Z are not acidic. Both SiCl4 and AlCl3 produce H+ ions in water, so both give a red colour with Universal Indicator.
